label: D-Link DGS-1520-28MP
description: D-Link DGS-1520-28MP (A1) - 28-port PoE Layer 3 stackable smart managed switch: 20x 10/100/1000BASE-T PoE RJ-45 plus 4x 2.5GBASE-T PoE RJ-45 on a 370 W budget (740 W with the DPS-700), 2x 10GBASE-T RJ-45 and 2x 10G SFP+ uplinks, 140 Gbps, 104.16 Mpps, RJ-45 console, 1U.

poe.note: IEEE 802.3af/at on all 24 copper ports (the datasheet lists the 10/100/1000Base-T PoE ports and the 2.5GBase-T PoE ports under one PoE standard row). Budget 370 W on the internal supply and 740 W with the optional DPS-700 redundant power supply fitted - the datasheet footnote says the DPS-700 only supports A2/B1 hardware, so on this A1 unit the 740 W figure is an upgrade path rather than a shipping number. 802.3af on every port is 369.6 W, which just fits inside 370 W, by 0.4 W. The per-port ceiling is the 802.3at Type-2 PSE figure of 30 W; the datasheet states the standard and the budget rather than a per-port wattage, and the budget, not the port count, is what binds.

fabric.note: Vendor switching capacity of 140 Gbps with a 104.16 Mpps maximum forwarding rate. The arithmetic checks out on a mixed-rate chassis: 20 gigabit plus 4 x 2.5G plus 2 x 10GBase-T plus 2 x 10G SFP+ is 20 x 2 + 4 x 5 + 4 x 20 = 140 Gbps full duplex.

notes: Ports, per the D-Link DGS-1520 Series A1 datasheet: 20 x 10/100/1000Base-T PoE, 4 x 2.5GBase-T PoE, 2 x 10GBase-T, 2 x 10G SFP+. All 24 copper ports are PoE at 802.3af/at - the 2.5G ports are not a separate PoE zone. The 2.5GBase-T ports are the reason this model exists: they take a Wi-Fi 6 access point above gigabit without a 10G run, and 802.3bz is in the standards list. The four ten-gigabit ports serve as stack links or uplinks. Maximum consumption 453.3 W with PoE on and 45.2 W with PoE off, standby 37.2 W at 100 V / 37.3 W at 240 V, heat 1545.8 BTU/hr, 57.1 dB(A), MTBF 333,946 hours, 441 x 308.5 x 44 mm (deeper than the non-PoE models because of the PoE supply), 4.29 kg. Takes the DPS-700 redundant AC supply for the 740 W figure. The datasheet does not publish a front-panel port index, so the ports are named by media (ge / mg / xgt / sfp+). Vendor software, same document: physical stacking of up to 8 units over 10GBase-T and/or SFP+ at up to 80 Gbps in ring or chain, virtual stacking (Single IP Management) of up to 32 units, 16,384 MAC entries (512 static), jumbo frames to 12,288 bytes, 32 LACP groups of 8 ports, 802.1D/802.1w/802.1s STP with BPDU filtering, root guard and loop guard, ERPS v1/v2, RSPAN, 4K VLAN groups (VID 1-4094) including selective Q-in-Q and VLAN translation, IGMP v1/v2/v3 snooping, MLD v1/v2 snooping, and L3 routing - static routes, RIP/RIPng, OSPF, VRRP v2/v3, PIM-SM/DM/SSM, 1024 hardware routing entries and 4096 L3 forwarding entries shared by IPv4/IPv6, 16 IP interfaces. Management: web GUI over IPv4/IPv6 with HTTPS, CLI, Telnet, SSH/SFTP, SNMP v1/v2c/v3, sFlow, RMON, LLDP/LLDP-MED, dual images and dual configuration files, ZTP and DHCP auto-configuration. Green: EEE, per-port power saving, time-based PoE (PoE models). Hardware Rev A1, 19-inch 1U, 100-240 VAC, operating range -5 to 50 C, EMI Class A.
